title: Termwise Tor acyclicity computes derived tensor
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and B a commutative R-algebra. A bounded cochain complex Q^\bullet of R-modules means R-modules Q^n with differentials d^n:Q^n\to Q^{n+1}, d^{n+1}d^n=0, and Q^n=0 for all but finitely many n. Assume Tor_i^R(Q^n,B)=0 for every n and every i>0, where Tor is the usual projective-resolution Tor [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Let Q^\bullet\otimes_R^L B denote the left-derived tensor product in the derived category of R-modules, and Q^\bullet\otimes_R B the ordinary total tensor complex. Then the canonical map Q^\bullet\otimes_R^L B\to Q^\bullet\otimes_R B is a quasi-isomorphism, and consequently H^i(Q^\bullet\otimes_R^L B)\cong H^i(Q^\bullet\otimes_R B) for every i.

source.place: Tag 08IB, lemma-compare-base-change: Tor-independent comparison of derived tensors

proof.text: Choose a and b with Q^n=0 outside [a,b]. For each n between a and b let sigma_{>=n}Q be the stupid truncation retaining Q^r for r>=n and putting zero below n. There is a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes 0 \to sigma_{>=n+1}Q \to sigma_{>=n}Q \to Q^n[-n] \to 0. This is obtained directly from the definitions: the first map is the inclusion, the second is projection to degree n, and the differential on the quotient is zero. The Tor-acyclicity hypothesis is inherited by every truncation term.

Notation for the derived tensor: apply [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to the one-point site with the ring map R\to B. It gives an exact functor -\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B:D(R)\to D(B), the left derived functor of the termwise tensor K(R)\to D(B), G\mapsto G\otimes_R B, computed by K-flat resolutions; the canonical map \tau_G:G\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B\to G\otimes_R B of the statement is the map induced by any K-flat resolution P\to G, namely P\otimes_R B\to G\otimes_R B. Restriction of scalars to R does not change cohomology, so it does not matter whether the comparison is read in D(B) or D(R). Base case: Q has one nonzero term, Q=Q^n[-n]. Choose a projective (hence flat) resolution F_\bullet\to Q^n and regard it, shifted, as a complex P concentrated in degrees at most n; P\to Q is a quasi-isomorphism and P is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Then \tau_Q is P\otimes_R B\to Q^n[-n]\otimes_R B, and H^{n-i}(P\otimes_R B)=Tor_i^R(Q^n,B) by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], with H^n mapping isomorphically to Q^n\otimes_R B (Tor_0=M\otimes N, right exactness). The hypothesis Tor_i^R(Q^n,B)=0 for i>0 says precisely that \tau_Q is a quasi-isomorphism. The case Q=0 is trivial.

Induction on the number of n with Q^n\neq0 (equivalently, descending n from b to a), the base case being the previous step. Put Q'=\sigma_{\ge n+1}Q, Q''=Q^n[-n] and Q=\sigma_{\ge n}Q, so 0\to Q'\to Q\to Q''\to0 is degreewise split (Step 1) and Q' has fewer nonzero terms. Its connecting map is the chain map c:Q''\to Q'[1] given by d^n:Q^n\to Q^{n+1} (up to the usual sign), so in K(R) it gives the triangle T: Q'\to Q\to Q''\xrightarrow{c}Q'[1], which is the distinguished triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] after passing to D(R). Apply the two functors F_1=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B and F_2=(termwise -\otimes_R B) from K(R) to D(B). F_1T is distinguished because -\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B is exact [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. F_2T is Q'\otimes B\to Q\otimes B\to Q''\otimes B\xrightarrow{c\otimes1}Q'[1]\otimes B, the triangle of the degreewise split (hence exact) sequence 0\to Q'\otimes_RB\to Q\otimes_RB\to Q''\otimes_RB\to0 with connecting map c\otimes1 [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], so it is distinguished. The comparison \tau is natural in G\in K(R) and compatible with the shift, since for a K-flat resolution P\to G the shift P[1]\to G[1] is a K-flat resolution and (P\otimes_RB)[1]=P[1]\otimes_RB termwise; hence (\tau_{Q'},\tau_Q,\tau_{Q''}) is a morphism of triangles F_1T\to F_2T [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-triangle-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder] it induces a morphism between the two long exact cohomology sequences. In the five-term segment H^{i-1}(Q'')\to H^i(Q')\to H^i(Q)\to H^i(Q'')\to H^{i+1}(Q') (with -\otimes^{\mathbf L}B above and -\otimes B below) the four outer vertical maps are isomorphisms, by the induction hypothesis for Q' and the base case for Q'', so H^i(\tau_Q) is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] in the abelian category of B-modules. Thus \tau_{\sigma_{\ge n}Q} is a quasi-isomorphism, and at n=a this is \tau_Q for the original Q.

proof.text: The map shown to be a quasi-isomorphism in the induction is \tau_Q, the canonical map Q\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B\to Q\otimes_RB of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; a quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all cohomology modules, giving H^i(Q\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\cong H^i(Q\otimes_RB) for every i.

lean.statement: theorem quasiIso_tensor_of_termwise_tor_acyclic {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (hbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (Q.X n)) (hTor : ∀ (n : ℤ) (i : ℕ), 0 < i → IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (Q.X n)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B))) (P : CochainComplex.KFlat (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (f : P.obj ⟶ Q) (hf : QuasiIso f) : QuasiIso ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f) ∧ ∀ i : ℤ, IsIso (homologyMap ((((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R B)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f) i)
lean.note: The canonical map is stated on an arbitrary K-flat resolution P.obj → Q, using the source repository’s CochainComplex.KFlat. Its tensor with B is the derived-to-ordinary comparison, read as complexes of R-modules as in the statement. No additional property of Q, R, or B is assumed.
